title: Declare per-endpoint SLOs with traffic-currency error-budgeting and regional graceful-shedding protocol
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Purpose:
This ticket defines a standardized per-endpoint SLO/SLI declaration format plus a novel 'traffic-currency' error-budget allocation model to enable predictable, auditable regional failover and prioritized graceful shedding. Goal is to unblock regional routing and eviction automation for multi-tenant endpoints while preserving premium customer contracts and minimizing user-visible regressions.

Scope and non-goals:
- In scope: SLI measurement definitions (latency, availability, correctness), per-endpoint SLO templates, traffic-currency allocation algorithm, circuit-breaker thresholds, load-shedding priority matrix, monitoring/alerting thresholds, runbook links, and required API flags for rollout gating.
- Out of scope: changes to client SDK routing; hardware procurement.

Key concepts:
1) Traffic-currency: assign each endpoint a daily "currency" budget derived from its declared SLOs and the endpoint's traffic mix. The currency is consumed when an endpoint breaches its per-region SLOs (burn) or when a region is used to serve fallback traffic from other regions (borrow). Currency accounting drives automated regional evictions and borrowing limits.
2) Graded graceful-shedding: eviction tiers (Tier 0: pinned/enterprise, Tier 1: standard paid, Tier 2: best-effort/free). Eviction proceeds by tier and by historical usage.
3) Model-variant fallback: when shedding, prefer lighter model variants (quantized or shorter context) before dropping requests.

Per-endpoint SLI/SLO templates (canonical):
- Availability (success): SLO = 99.95% monthly availability; SLI = count(successful 2xx/streaming-OK responses) / count(attempts) excluding client-cancelled requests. Measurement window: rolling 30d and calendar 30d for billing.
- Latency (p95): SLO = p95 < 220ms (short-context routes), p95 < 400ms (long-context routes). SLI = server-to-first-byte latency measured at edge hop (intra-region) excluding queued time if queue>500ms.
- Tail-latency (p99): SLO = maintain p99 < 1200ms for priority routes.
- Correctness/Quality (regression signal): SLO = no more than 2% of nightly eval promptset fails acceptance thresholds (see acceptance_criteria).
- Error budget: derived from 1 - SLO. Example: monthly availability 99.95% -> budget = ~21.6 minutes of downtime.

Traffic-currency allocation algorithm (summary):
- Base currency = endpoint_daily_QPS_weight * endpoint_error_budget_fraction * scaling_factor.
- QPS_weight is a function of recent 7d traffic and customer tier weighting.
- Currency is tracked per-region and global borrowing is permitted up to 15% of global currency for emergencies.
- Exhaustion policy: when regional currency < 5% remaining, trigger pre-emptive borrowing and raise a Severity-2 alert to SRE.

Circuit-breaker and failover policy:
- Circuit states: CLOSED -> PROBATION -> OPEN -> DEGRADATION -> CLOSED.
- Entry conditions: region OPEN when p95 latency > 2x SLO for 5m AND error-rate > threshold (1% for premium endpoints, 3% for standard).
- Probation window: 10m with sampled traffic at 5% of QPS to validate recovery.
- Automatic regional ejection: if OPEN persists for 15m and currency borrow limit exceeded, route 100% of new traffic to secondary regions with warm fallbacks.

Load-shedding rules (priority-based):
1) Admission control: per-host queue limiter with token-bucket for request admission.
2) Eviction order: Tier 2 best-effort -> optional-retry low-priority routes -> Tier 1 standard (only degrade model variant) -> Tier 0 pinned (avoid eviction; if necessary, coordinated paid-path fallback to Dedicated).
3) Degradation steps: reduce max-context by 50% -> switch to quantized model variant -> sample-only responses (return cached summaries) -> hard-fail with graceful error explaining degraded mode.
4) Safety caps: never evict pinned endpoints without manual approval unless a cross-region outage is ongoing and Service Health <= 75%.

Observability and alerts:
- Dashboards: per-endpoint SLO dashboard (p95, p99, availability, budget burn rate). Reference: https://app.redwood.internal/dashboards/slo/ENG-472019
- Alerting:
  - SLO burn-rate alert: when 3h burn rate predicts > 50% of monthly budget consumed -> P2.
  - Regional ejection alert: region circuit OPEN -> P1.
  - Currency-exhaustion alert: regional currency < 5% -> P1.

Runbooks and links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/traffic-currency-slo-spec
- Implementation RFC: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/142
- GitHub PR for measurement shim: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/11023
- Canary dashboard: https://app.redwood.internal/dashboards/canary/traffic-currency
- Postmortem reference (incident-2025-11): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INC/2025-11-multiregion-failover

Rollout plan and gating:
- Phase 1 (canary): enable traffic-currency accounting for 5 internal endpoints (2 weeks). Canary gate: no canary endpoint has >20% monthly budget burn in first 72h.
- Phase 2 (limited): opt-in for 10 customers across regions; run for 3 weeks. Gate: automated regional ejection succeeded without customer-visible degradation in 95% of test runs.
- Phase 3: rollout to all hosted endpoints behind feature-flag; enable automated shedding. Gate: stability metrics and SRE sign-off.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- SLI measurement implemented and validated against synthetic traffic (links in attachments).
- Traffic-currency counters exposed in Console for each endpoint and region.
- Automated circuit-breaker transitions produce expected routing changes in canaries.
- Runbook drafted and exercised in SRE runbook drills.

Implementation notes and tradeoffs:
- Tradeoff: aggressive shedding reduces cost but risks degraded UX. We prefer multi-step degradation to preserve meaningful responses.
- Tradeoff: currency accounting complexity vs. operational visibility. Start with daily buckets and 7d smoothing; revisit hourly slabs if needed.
- Privacy: currency accounting is metadata-only; no content inspected. Security review required for any telemetry changes.
